content.title: Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani on Instagram: "Happy St. Patrick’s Day, New York."
content.text: Happy St. Patrick’s Day, New York.That’s my mayor!! (I live in Dublin)It should not feel so strange to listen to so many coherent sentences in a row 🤯Is it normal to get emotional about coherent sentences and decency?It is amazing and wild that @nycmayor just educated more Americans aboit Irish history in one reel than the entire American and British esucation system combined, education systems that serve Irish people and peoole of Irish descent.Irish support for Palestine is deeply rooted in a shared history of colonialism, oppression, and conflict, leading many Irish people to identify with the Palestinian struggle as an "underdog" against a dominant power. As a former British colony, Ireland draws parallels between its experience with British occupation and the Palestinian situationMy immigrant Irish father helped build the stairs in the Twin Towers. Mayor you make me proud to have been born and raised in NYC🇮🇪☘️Our revenge will be the laughter of our children! - Bobby Sands 🇮🇪💚Taking a moment on St. Paddy’s to actually honor the Irish people and their struggle? Hell yes ☘️Éirinn go BráchConvenient you told us a history lesson and didn’t make any mention of contemporary politics.As an Irish person, this makes me feel properly seen by a US politician for the first time in my 53 years. You don’t even have a direct personal link to Ireland and yet you are so knowledgeable and well informed about both our past and recent history as well as the contribution our small island has made to the US and the world. Go raibh míle agat, Árdmheara Mamdani! 👏As a Mexican-American I celebrate St.Patrick’s Day in Honor of the San Patricios (St. Patrick's Battalion). They helped defend my parent’s homeland against unjust invasion and for religious freedom.This made me tear up 🇮🇪💚This is sooo interesting! I cannot believe the history of St Patrick is this rich and today it is mostly a drinking holidayHonestly, he gives me so much hope that people who actually care can be in positions of power and influence.
